learningGoals: Understand and talk about the five senses, focusing on touch, smell, and hearing. 👂
Learn and use descriptive adjectives for textures, sounds, and smells. 🌸
Follow simple auditory instructions without relying on visual cues. 🧭
Develop empathy and awareness of how people navigate the world differently. 🤝
Read short phrases that describe sensory experiences with proper intonation. 📖
conversationStarters: If you closed your eyes, how would you know that dinner is cooking in the kitchen? 🍲
What is the softest thing in your bedroom, and what does it feel like against your skin? 🧸
Can you close your eyes right now and tell me three sounds you can hear? 🎶
teachingTips: Play blindfold games safely in a clear area to help them focus on their other senses. 🧣
Introduce opposing descriptive words in pairs, like soft/hard, loud/quiet, to build their vocabulary faster. ⚖️
While reading the chapter, pause and ask them to imagine the smell or sound described in the text. 💭
Discuss how our ears, hands, and nose help keep us safe, like smelling smoke or hearing a car. 🚨
Practice spelling sensory words by writing them in sand or sugar using their fingers to feel the letters. ✍️

funActivities.title: Mystery Touch Bag 🛍️
funActivities.description: Place different items like a cotton ball, a rock, a leaf, and a coin in a bag. Have your child close their eyes, reach in, and describe how the item feels before guessing what it is.

funActivities.title: Sound Safari Walk 🚶‍♀️
funActivities.description: Go for a short walk and agree to be perfectly quiet. Listen for birds, cars, wind, or footsteps. Afterwards, talk about all the loud and quiet things you heard.

funActivities.title: Smell and Tell 🍋
funActivities.description: Blindfold your child and hold safe, familiar scents under their nose, like a lemon, a flower, cinnamon, or soap. Have them guess the smell and describe it.
